questions.question: For binary $y_1,y_2$ ($y_j=1$ means decision $j$ is yes), what requirement does the constraint $y_2\le y_1$ express?
options: Decision 2 may be yes only if decision 1 is yes
Decision 2 must be yes whenever decision 1 is no
Decisions 1 and 2 may never both be yes at once
Decision 2 must be yes whenever decision 1 is yes

questions.question: For binary $y_1,y_2$ ($y_j=1$ means decision $j$ is yes), which combination $(y_1,y_2)$ does the constraint $y_2\le y_1$ rule out?
A model writes $y_2\le y_1$ for the rule that decision 2 needs decision 1, but only imposes the bounds $0\le y_1,y_2\le1$. What does this permit?
options: Nothing extra, since $y_2\le y_1$ forces $y_1,y_2$ to be $0$ or $1$
Only $y_2=1$ with $y_1=0$, the pair that was meant to be ruled out
Only values with $y_1=y_2$, since fractions must cancel out
Half decisions such as $y_1=y_2=0.5$, which satisfy $y_2\le y_1$

questions.question: Under the requirement $y_1+y_2\ge1$ on binary $y_1,y_2$ ($y_j=1$ means decision $j$ is yes), which outcome becomes impossible?
options: Decision 2 alone yes: $(y_1,y_2)=(0,1)$
Both decisions no: $(y_1,y_2)=(0,0)$
Both decisions yes: $(y_1,y_2)=(1,1)$
Decision 1 alone yes: $(y_1,y_2)=(1,0)$

questions.question: For binary $y_1,y_2$ ($y_j=1$ means decision $j$ is yes), how does the constraint $y_1\le y_2$ read in words?
options: Decision 2 can only follow a yes on decision 1
Choosing decision 2 obliges the firm to take decision 1 too
Decision 1 is allowed only when decision 2 is yes
Decision 1 and decision 2 must always be the same

questions.question: A firm may open a cafe ($y_c=1$) only if it leases a shop unit ($y_s=1$); $y_c,y_s$ are binary. Which constraint models this?
options: $y_c\le y_s$
$y_s\le y_c$
$y_c+y_s\le1$
$y_c=y_s$

questions.question: For binary $y_1,y_2$ ($y_j=1$ means decision $j$ is yes), a model contains $y_2\le y_1$. Management has already fixed decision 2 as yes, so $y_2=1$. Which values of $y_1$ does the constraint still allow?
options: Both $y_1=0$ and $y_1=1$: decision 1 is not restricted
No value: $1\le y_1$ fails for a binary $y_1$, so no plan exists
Only $y_1=0$: the two decisions cannot both be yes
Only $y_1=1$: decision 2 yes forces decision 1 yes

questions.question: A campaign ($y_3=1$) may run only if both a product launch ($y_1=1$) and a website ($y_2=1$) go ahead; all are binary. Which model is correct?
options: $y_3\le y_1$ and $y_3\le y_2$

questions.question: A model for binary $y_1,y_2,y_3$ ($y_j=1$ means decision $j$ is yes) has $y_3\le y_1$ and $y_3\le y_2$. Which selection $(y_1,y_2,y_3)$ violates it?
Decision 1 has value $-2$ and decision 2 has value $7$; with binary $y_1,y_2$ ($y_j=1$ means decision $j$ is yes) and $y_2\le y_1$, maximize $-2y_1+7y_2$. What is the optimal value?
At each of two locations $i$, a warehouse ($W_i=1$) may be built only if a factory is built there ($F_i=1$); all are binary. Why not just impose $W_1+W_2\le F_1+F_2$?
options: It forbids building two factories when there is one warehouse
It allows a warehouse at one site and the factory at the other
It is nonlinear, while the per-location version is linear
It allows a warehouse at a place where no factory exists at all

questions.question: For binary $y_1,y_2,y_3$ ($y_j=1$ means decision $j$ is yes), a model has $y_3\le y_2$ and $y_2\le y_1$. A planner wants to add $y_3\le y_1$. What does adding it change?
options: It newly excludes $(0,1,1)$, where only decision 1 is no
It forces decision 3 to be yes whenever decision 1 is yes
Nothing: the chain $y_3\le y_2\le y_1$ already implies it
It cuts off $(1,0,1)$, a plan that the chain still permits

questions.question: For binary $y_1,y_2$ ($y_j=1$ means decision $j$ is yes), a model contains both $y_2\le y_1$ and $y_1\le y_2$. What does this pair of constraints require?
options: At most one of the two decisions can be yes
The two decisions are taken together or not at all
At least one of the two decisions must be yes
The two constraints cancel, so any pair is allowed

questions.question: A council either renovates its town hall ($y_1=1$) or, if it does not renovate, must relocate ($y_2=1$); $y_1,y_2$ are binary. Which constraint models the requirement?
Projects A, B, C have values $6$, $10$, $7$ and costs $5$, $4$, $3$; the budget is $9$, and B may be chosen only if A is chosen. What is the highest total value?
Project 3 may go ahead only if project 1 or project 2 (or both) goes ahead; binary $y_j=1$ means project $j$ goes ahead. Which single constraint models this?
For binary $y_1,y_2$ ($y_j=1$ means decision $j$ is yes), which statement is equivalent to the constraint $y_2\le y_1$?
For binary $y_1,y_2,y_3$ ($y_j=1$ means decision $j$ is yes), the constraint $y_1-y_2+y_3\le1$ models: if $y_1=1$ and $y_2=0$, then $y_3=0$. Which selections with $y_1=0$ does it rule out?
options: $(0,1,1)$, since $y_2$ and $y_3$ cannot both be $1$
None: with $y_1=0$ the left side is at most $1$
$(0,0,0)$, since some decision must be yes

questions.question: For binary $y_1,y_2,y_3$ ($y_j=1$ means decision $j$ is yes), a student replaces $y_3\le y_1$ and $y_3\le y_2$ by the single constraint $2y_3\le y_1+y_2$. Is this a correct model of: decision 3 only if both decisions 1 and 2 are yes?
options: Yes: for $y_j\in\{0,1\}$ it allows exactly the same selections
No: it still allows $y_3=1$ when only one of $y_1,y_2$ is $1$
No: it forbids $y_3=1$ even when $y_1$ and $y_2$ are both $1$
No: it forces $y_3=1$ as soon as $y_1$ and $y_2$ are both $1$

questions.question: For binary $y_1,y_2,y_3$ ($y_j=1$ means decision $j$ is yes), which constraint rules out exactly the selections where $y_1=1$, $y_2=0$ and $y_3=1$?
